psnr or ssim (default psnr) - Metric the encoder optimises for; ssim scales RD per block and often looks better
default, screen or film (default default) - Content hint; screen suits desktop capture, film retains grain
0-7 (default 0) - Keeps fine detail by curbing coefficient and skip optimisation, costing PSNR and bitrate
0 or higher (default 0 off) - Codes low-motion blocks as skip below this distortion; speeds up real-time
0-1 (default 0) - Allows periodic frame-level Q boosts, spending bits where they help most on calm content
0-6 (default 1) - Alt reference frames; 2 and above enables multi-layer ARF, usually a quality gain
0-25 (default 25) - Lookahead depth; more improves alt-ref placement, 0 gives low delay at a quality cost
0-15 (default 7) - Frames blended by the alt-ref temporal filter; lower keeps grain, higher denoises more
0-6 (default 5) - Alt-ref filter strength; drop to 1-2 to preserve film grain, raise for noisy sources
0-1 (default 0) - Extra adaptive quantisation on alt-ref frames; skipped at low bitrates where it costs more
0-1 (default 1) - Frame parallel decodability; 0 allows backward probability updates and compresses better
0-4 (default 0 off) - Adaptive quantisation: 1 variance, 2 complexity, 3 cyclic refresh, 4 equator360
0-63 (default 0) - Best quantiser allowed; raise it to stop easy scenes from soaking up bitrate
0-63 (default 63) - Worst quantiser allowed; lower it to keep hard scenes from collapsing in VBR encodes
0-1 (default 1) - Temporal dependency model; improves bit allocation between frames, disable only to save time
0-10000 (default 0 off) - Corpus VBR complexity midpoint; holds quality steady across a library of clips
0-100 (default 25) - How far under target rate a section may run; higher lets easy scenes save more bits
0-100 (default 25) - How far over target rate a section may run; higher lets hard scenes spend more bits
